root.label: Principles of Neural Science
root.summary: A comprehensive textbook covering the field of neuroscience, now in its sixth edition.

core_concepts.label: Core Concepts of Neuroscience
core_concepts.summary: Fundamental areas of study within the field of neuroscience.

cellular_neuroscience.label: Cellular Neuroscience
cellular_neuroscience.summary: The study of the structure, function, and properties of neurons and glial cells.

neuron_structure.label: Neuron Structure
neuron_structure.summary: The anatomical components of a neuron, including dendrites, soma, axon, and synapses.

ion_channels.label: Ion Channels
ion_channels.summary: Transmembrane proteins that allow specific ions to pass through the cell membrane, crucial for neuronal signaling.

action_potentials.label: Action Potentials
action_potentials.summary: Rapid, transient changes in the membrane potential of a neuron, enabling long-distance communication.

synaptic_transmission.label: Synaptic Transmission
synaptic_transmission.summary: The process by which signals are transmitted from one neuron to another at a synapse.

developmental_neuroscience.label: Developmental Neuroscience
developmental_neuroscience.summary: The study of how the nervous system develops from conception to maturity.

neural_induction.label: Neural Induction
neural_induction.summary: The process by which cells are committed to becoming neurons.

neuronal_migration.label: Neuronal Migration
neuronal_migration.summary: The movement of neurons to their final destinations in the developing nervous system.

synaptogenesis.label: Synaptogenesis
synaptogenesis.summary: The formation of synapses between neurons.

neural_pruning.label: Neural Pruning
neural_pruning.summary: The elimination of unnecessary neurons and synapses.

systems_neuroscience.label: Systems Neuroscience
systems_neuroscience.summary: The study of how neural circuits and systems process information.

sensory_systems.label: Sensory Systems
sensory_systems.summary: Neural pathways responsible for processing sensory information (e.g., vision, hearing, touch).

motor_systems.label: Motor Systems
motor_systems.summary: Neural pathways responsible for controlling movement.

limbic_system.label: Limbic System
limbic_system.summary: A set of brain structures involved in emotion, motivation, and memory.

cognitive_neuroscience.label: Cognitive Neuroscience
cognitive_neuroscience.summary: The study of the neural basis of cognitive processes, such as attention, memory, and language.

behavioral_neuroscience.label: Behavioral Neuroscience
behavioral_neuroscience.summary: The study of the neural basis of behavior.

copyright_info.summary: Copyright © 2021 by McGraw Hill. All rights reserved.

dedication.label: Dedication
dedication.summary: Dedicated to Thomas M. Jessell and Sarah H. Mack.

thomas_jessell.label: Thomas M. Jessell
thomas_jessell.summary: A neuroscientist who made pioneering contributions to spinal cord development and motor control (1951-2019).

sarah_mack.label: Sarah H. Mack
sarah_mack.summary: Art editor and contributor to the book for over 30 years, responsible for the visual design (1962-2020).

part_i.label: Part I: Overall Perspective
part_i.summary: Provides a broad overview of the themes of neural science, including the anatomical organization of the nervous system and the genetic bases of behavior.

chapter_1.label: Chapter 1: The Brain and Behavior
chapter_1.summary: Explores the relationship between brain structure and function, and how it gives rise to behavior.

chapter_2.label: Chapter 2: Genes and Behavior
chapter_2.summary: Discusses the genetic influences on nervous system function and behavior.

chapter_3.label: Chapter 3: Nerve Cells, Neural Circuitry, and Behavior
chapter_3.summary: Examines the role of nerve cells and their connections in mediating behavior.

chapter_4.label: Chapter 4: The Neuroanatomical Bases by Which Neural Circuits Mediate Behavior
chapter_4.summary: Details the neuroanatomical structures that underpin neural circuit function and behavior.

chapter_5.label: Chapter 5: The Computational Bases of Neural Circuits That Mediate Behavior
chapter_5.summary: Introduces the computational principles by which neurons participate in neural circuits to perform specific computations relevant to behavior. Includes new experimental technologies like optogenetics and chemogenetics.

chapter_6.label: Chapter 6: Imaging and Behavior
chapter_6.summary: Considers how modern imaging techniques applied to the human brain bridge neuroscience and psychology.

part_ii.label: Part II: Cell and Molecular Biology of Cells of the Nervous System
part_ii.summary: Focuses on the basic properties of nerve cells, including the generation and conduction of the action potential.

chapter_7.label: Chapter 7: The Cells of the Nervous System
chapter_7.summary: Describes the different types of cells that make up the nervous system.

chapter_8.label: Chapter 8: Ion Channels
chapter_8.summary: Details the structure and function of ion channels, crucial for neuronal signaling.

chapter_9.label: Chapter 9: Membrane Potential and the Passive Electrical Properties of the Neuron
chapter_9.summary: Explains the concepts of membrane potential and passive electrical properties of neurons.

chapter_10.label: Chapter 10: Propagated Signaling: The Action Potential
chapter_10.summary: Describes the generation and propagation of action potentials.

part_iii.label: Part III: Synaptic Transmission
part_iii.summary: Focuses on the electrophysiological and molecular mechanisms of synaptic transmission.

chapter_11.label: Chapter 11: Overview of Synaptic Transmission
chapter_11.summary: Provides a general overview of the process of synaptic transmission.

chapter_12.label: Chapter 12: Directly Gated Transmission: The Nerve-Muscle Synapse
chapter_12.summary: Details the mechanisms of synaptic transmission at the nerve-muscle synapse.

chapter_13.label: Chapter 13: Synaptic Integration in the Central Nervous System
chapter_13.summary: Explains how synaptic inputs are integrated in the central nervous system.

chapter_14.label: Chapter 14: Modulation of Synaptic Transmission and Neuronal Excitability: Second Messengers
chapter_14.summary: Describes how synaptic transmission and neuronal excitability are modulated by second messengers.

chapter_15.label: Chapter 15: Transmitter Release
chapter_15.summary: Details the mechanisms of neurotransmitter release.

chapter_16.label: Chapter 16: Neurotransmitters
chapter_16.summary: Describes the different types of neurotransmitters and their functions.

part_iv.label: Part IV: Perception
part_iv.summary: Discusses the neural mechanisms underlying sensory perception.

part_v.label: Part V: Movement
part_v.summary: Covers the neural mechanisms underlying movement.

part_vi.label: Part VI: The Biology of Emotion, Motivation, and Homeostasis
part_vi.summary: Explores the neural mechanisms underlying emotion, motivation, and homeostasis.

part_vii.label: Part VII: Development and the Emergence of Behavior
part_vii.summary: Discusses the development of the nervous system and its impact on behavior.

part_viii.label: Part VIII: Learning, Memory, Language and Cognition
part_viii.summary: Covers the neural mechanisms underlying learning, memory, language, and cognition.

part_ix.label: Part IX: Diseases of the Nervous System
part_ix.summary: Discusses the neural mechanisms underlying diseases of the nervous system.

tom_influence.label: Tom's Influence
tom_influence.summary: Tom Kandel's influence on the field of neuroscience and the Principles book, despite facing a neurodegenerative disease in his later years. He encouraged rigor in language and prose.

brain_imaging.label: Invasive Brain Imaging
brain_imaging.summary: Techniques that allow scientists to identify brain areas activated during cognitive acts. Includes electrode implantation for electrophysiological recordings and neural stimulation.

electrophysiological_recordings.label: Electrophysiological Recordings
electrophysiological_recordings.summary: Recording electrical activity of neurons using implanted electrodes.

neural_stimulation.label: Local Neural Stimulation
neural_stimulation.summary: Stimulating neurons in specific brain areas using implanted electrodes.

brain_machine_interface.label: Brain-Machine Interface (BMI)
brain_machine_interface.summary: Technology that creates a direct communication pathway between the brain and an external device. (Chapter 39)

neural_mechanisms.label: Neural Mechanisms
neural_mechanisms.summary: Understanding basic and higher-order neural mechanisms is crucial for understanding both normal brain function and neurological/psychiatric disorders.

higher_order_neural_mechanisms.label: Higher-Order Neural Mechanisms
higher_order_neural_mechanisms.summary: Complex processes involving interactions between multiple neural systems.

genetic_influences.label: Genetic Influences
genetic_influences.summary: Inherited or spontaneous mutations in neuronally expressed genes contribute to brain disease.

inherited_mutations.label: Inherited Mutations
inherited_mutations.summary: Genetic mutations passed down from parents that can contribute to brain disease.

spontaneous_mutations.label: Spontaneous Mutations
spontaneous_mutations.summary: Mutations that occur randomly during development or throughout life that can contribute to brain disease.

environmental_factors.label: Environmental Factors
environmental_factors.summary: Environmental factors interact with genetic mechanisms to influence disease progression.

neurological_disorders.label: Neurological Disorders
neurological_disorders.summary: Diseases affecting the nervous system, including neurodegenerative diseases.

neurodegenerative_diseases.label: Neurodegenerative Diseases
neurodegenerative_diseases.summary: Diseases characterized by the progressive loss of structure or function of neurons, such as Parkinson's and Alzheimer's disease.

alzheimers_disease.label: Alzheimer's Disease
alzheimers_disease.summary: A neurodegenerative disorder affecting memory and cognitive function.

neurodevelopmental_disorders.label: Neurodevelopmental Disorders
neurodevelopmental_disorders.summary: Disorders that affect the development of the nervous system, such as schizophrenia and autism.

schizophrenia.label: Schizophrenia
schizophrenia.summary: A chronic mental disorder affecting a person's ability to think, feel, and behave clearly.

autism.label: Autism
autism.summary: A developmental disability that affects how a person interacts with others, communicates, learns, and behaves.

historical_perspective.label: Historical Perspective
historical_perspective.summary: Studies of brain disease provide insights into normal brain function, including memory and consciousness.

memory.label: Memory
memory.summary: The process of encoding, storing, and retrieving information.

consciousness.label: Consciousness
consciousness.summary: The state of being aware of and responsive to one's surroundings.

future_directions.label: Future Directions
future_directions.summary: The field of neuroscience faces challenges and opportunities for future research.

critical_thinking.label: Critical Thinking
critical_thinking.summary: Encouraging questioning of established knowledge to drive further discovery.

experimental_approaches.label: Experimental Approaches
experimental_approaches.summary: Developing and refining experimental methods to address fundamental questions in neuroscience.

contributors.label: Contributors
contributors.summary: List of researchers who contributed to the field.

movement_intro.label: Introduction to Movement
movement_intro.summary: Overview of the motor system and its importance in animal life.

movement_definition.label: Definition of Movement
movement_definition.summary: Movement is a defining feature of animal life.

motor_system_function.label: Motor System Function
motor_system_function.summary: The motor system controls coordinated, purposeful movements.

motor_vs_sensory.label: Motor vs. Sensory Systems
motor_vs_sensory.summary: Motor systems begin with an internal representation of desired movement, while sensory systems create an internal representation of the external world.

movement_control.label: Movement Control
movement_control.summary: Movement control requires continuous updating with internal (efference copy) and external sensory information.

psychophysical_analysis.label: Psychophysical Analysis
psychophysical_analysis.summary: Psychophysical analyses reveal the control rules used by the motor system.

motor_hierarchy.label: Motor Hierarchy
motor_hierarchy.summary: A functional hierarchy of motor control, involving the prefrontal cortex, posterior parietal cortex, premotor cortex, primary motor cortex, brainstem, and spinal cord.

prefrontal_cortex.label: Prefrontal Cortex
prefrontal_cortex.summary: Highest level of motor hierarchy, dealing with the purpose of movement.

posterior_parietal_cortex.label: Posterior Parietal Cortex
posterior_parietal_cortex.summary: Involved in the formation of motor plans, interacting with the premotor cortex.

premotor_cortex.label: Premotor Cortex
premotor_cortex.summary: Specifies spatiotemporal characteristics of movements based on sensory information.

primary_motor_cortex.label: Primary Motor Cortex
primary_motor_cortex.summary: Coordinates spatiotemporal details of muscle contractions.

motor_learning.label: Motor Learning
motor_learning.summary: A fruitful subject for studies of neural plasticity.

transmitter_systems.label: Neurotransmitter Systems
transmitter_systems.summary: Specific transmitter systems (e.g., dopamine) play a critical role in action selection and reinforcement.

dopamine_basal_ganglia.label: Dopamine & Basal Ganglia
dopamine_basal_ganglia.summary: Deficiency in dopamine in the basal ganglia is linked to Parkinson's disease.

brain_machine_interfaces.label: Brain-Machine Interfaces (BMIs)
brain_machine_interfaces.summary: Devices that measure or alter electrophysiological activity to restore lost capabilities.

bmi_categories.label: BMI Categories
bmi_categories.summary: BMIs can be categorized by the function they restore: sensory, motor, regulation of pathological activity, or brain processing.

sensory_bmi.label: Sensory BMIs
sensory_bmi.summary: Restore lost sensory capabilities (e.g., cochlear implants, retinal prostheses).

cochlear_implants.label: Cochlear Implants
cochlear_implants.summary: Restore hearing by electrically stimulating spiral ganglion cells in the cochlea.

retinal_prostheses.label: Retinal Prostheses
retinal_prostheses.summary: Restore vision by electrically stimulating retinal ganglion cells.

motor_bmi.label: Motor BMIs
motor_bmi.summary: Restore lost motor capabilities (e.g., assisting paralyzed people and amputees).

pathological_bmi.label: Pathological BMIs
pathological_bmi.summary: Regulate pathological neural activity (e.g., deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's disease).

deep_brain_stimulation.label: Deep Brain Stimulation
deep_brain_stimulation.summary: Focal stimulation of the basal ganglia to restore motility in Parkinson's disease.

bmi_measurement.label: BMI Measurement
bmi_measurement.summary: BMIs measure neural activity using advanced neurotechnology.

bmi_modulation.label: BMI Modulation
bmi_modulation.summary: BMIs modulate neural activity to restore function.

neural_recording.label: Neural Recording
neural_recording.summary: Measuring electrical neural activity using penetrating multi-electrode arrays.

electrode_arrays.label: Electrode Arrays
electrode_arrays.summary: Arrays of electrodes implanted in brain regions to record neural activity. (e.g., primary motor cortex, dorsal and ventral premotor cortex, intraparietal cortex).

local_field_potentials.label: Local Field Potentials (LFPs)
local_field_potentials.summary: Lower-frequency signals recorded from the same electrodes as action potentials, believed to arise from synaptic currents of many nearby neurons.

neural_decoding.label: Neural Decoding
neural_decoding.summary: Predicting desired movements from neural activity using statistical procedures.

bmi_operation.label: BMI Operation
bmi_operation.summary: Real-time measurement of neural activity, decoding of desired movements, and use of decoded movements to control devices.

prosthetic_devices.label: Prosthetic Devices
prosthetic_devices.summary: External devices controlled by decoded movements, such as computer cursors or robotic arms.

functional_electrical_stimulation.label: Functional Electrical Stimulation (FES)
functional_electrical_stimulation.summary: Electrically stimulating muscles in a paralyzed limb to enact decoded movements.

feedback_control.label: Closed-Loop Feedback Control
feedback_control.summary: Altering neural activity based on feedback from prosthetic devices to improve accuracy. Can utilize visual and non-visual sensory modalities.

surrogate_sensory_information.label: Surrogate Sensory Information
surrogate_sensory_information.summary: Providing sensory feedback (e.g., pressure, position) from prosthetic devices via electrical stimulation to proprioceptive and somatosensory cortex.

bmi_types.label: BMI Types
bmi_types.summary: Categorization of BMIs based on their primary function.

motor_bmis.label: Motor BMIs
motor_bmis.summary: BMIs designed to provide natural control of robotic or paralyzed limbs.

communication_bmis.label: Communication BMIs
communication_bmis.summary: BMIs designed to provide a fast and accurate interface with electronic devices (e.g., computers, smartphones).

pathological_regulation.label: Regulation of Pathological Neural Activity
pathological_regulation.summary: Using BMIs to treat disorders involving aberrant neural activity, such as Parkinson's disease and epilepsy.

antiseizure_bmis.label: Antiseizure BMIs
antiseizure_bmis.summary: Continuously monitoring neural activity to predict and disrupt seizure onset through electrical stimulation.

replacement_parts.label: Replacement Part BMIs
replacement_parts.summary: Restoring lost brain processing capabilities by replacing damaged brain regions with electronic hardware and software.

neurotechnology.label: Neurotechnology
neurotechnology.summary: The broad area of electronic technologies applied to the nervous system for measuring and modulating neural activity.

sensor_types.label: Neural Sensors
sensor_types.summary: Different types of sensors used to measure neural signals, categorized by invasiveness and spatial resolution.

eeg.label: Electroencephalography (EEG)
eeg.summary: Non-invasive technique measuring electrical activity via electrodes on the scalp. Measures average activity from many neurons.

eeg_fact_1.label: EEG Characteristics
eeg_fact_1.summary: EEG uses metal disks (electrodes) applied to the scalp to detect average neuronal activity.

ecog.label: Electrocorticography (ECoG)
ecog.summary: Implantable technique measuring electrical activity on the surface of the brain. Higher spatial and temporal resolution than EEG.

ecog_fact_1.label: ECoG Characteristics
ecog_fact_1.summary: ECoG electrodes are placed on the brain's surface, closer to neurons than EEG electrodes, resulting in higher resolution.

intracortical_electrodes.label: Intracortical Electrodes
intracortical_electrodes.summary: Implantable electrodes penetrating into the cortex. Record action potentials from individual neurons and local field potentials.

intracortical_fact_1.label: Intracortical Electrode Construction
intracortical_fact_1.summary: Made of silicon or other biocompatible materials, penetrating 1-2mm into the cortex.

intracortical_fact_2.label: Intracortical Electrode Recording Capabilities
intracortical_fact_2.summary: Record action potentials from individual neurons and local field potentials from small clusters.

technological_challenges.label: Technological Challenges in BMIs
technological_challenges.summary: Key areas of development for improving BMI performance.

scaling_neurons.label: Scaling Neuron Measurement
scaling_neurons.summary: Increasing the number of neurons measured simultaneously to improve BMI control.

scaling_neurons_fact_1.label: Neuron Scaling Requirements
scaling_neurons_fact_1.summary: Tens to hundreds of neurons are needed for natural BMI movement, and even more for naturalistic motor function.

low_power_electronics.label: Low-Power Electronics
low_power_electronics.summary: Developing electronics for signal acquisition, wireless communication, and powering with minimal energy consumption.

low_power_fact_1.label: Low Power Requirements
low_power_fact_1.summary: Minimizing power consumption reduces battery size/replacement frequency and prevents brain overheating.

low_power_fact_2.label: BMI System Evolution
low_power_fact_2.summary: Future BMIs will be fully implanted like DBS systems, requiring fully integrated electronics.

supervisory_systems.label: Supervisory Systems
supervisory_systems.summary: Software for managing BMI operation, including monitoring user intent, recalibrating decoders, and ensuring safety.

supervisory_fact_1.label: Supervisory System Functions
supervisory_fact_1.summary: Software monitors user intent (e.g., sleep), neural signal changes, and overall BMI performance.

decoding_algorithms.label: Movement Decoding Algorithms
decoding_algorithms.summary: Algorithms used to estimate desired movement from neural activity.

movement_encoding.label: Movement Encoding
movement_encoding.summary: Aspects of movement (position, velocity, etc.) are encoded in neuronal activity.

spike_histograms.label: Spike Histograms
spike_histograms.summary: Averaged neuronal activity across multiple trials to characterize neuron response to a target.

spike_histogram_fact_1.label: Spike Histogram Use
spike_histogram_fact_1.summary: Comparing spike histograms for different targets reveals how neuron activity varies with movement.

tuning_curves.label: Tuning Curves
tuning_curves.summary: Represent the relationship between neuron activity and movement direction (often a cosine function).

tuning_curve_fact_1.label: Tuning Curve Interpretation
tuning_curve_fact_1.summary: A neuron's firing rate at a specific level can indicate potential movement direction.

single_neuron_encoding.label: Single Neuron Encoding
single_neuron_encoding.summary: Analyzing the activity of individual neurons related to movement.

neuron_tuning_curve.label: Neuron Tuning Curve
neuron_tuning_curve.summary: The relationship between a neuron's firing rate and movement parameters (e.g., direction).

ambiguity_in_direction.label: Directional Ambiguity
ambiguity_in_direction.summary: A single neuron's activity can correspond to multiple movement directions (e.g., 120° or 240°).

preparation_activity.label: Preparation Activity
preparation_activity.summary: Neural activity occurring *before* the execution of a movement.

execution_activity.label: Execution Activity
execution_activity.summary: Neural activity occurring *during* the execution of a movement.

multiple_neuron_encoding.label: Multiple Neuron Encoding
multiple_neuron_encoding.summary: Using the combined activity of multiple neurons to represent movement.

improved_accuracy.label: Improved Accuracy with Multiple Neurons
improved_accuracy.summary: Combining information from multiple neurons reduces ambiguity and improves movement decoding accuracy.

movement_decoding.label: Movement Decoding
movement_decoding.summary: Extracting movement information from neural activity.

single_trial_decoding.label: Single Trial Decoding
single_trial_decoding.summary: Decoding movement information from the activity of many neurons on a single trial.

averaged_trial_decoding.label: Averaged Trial Decoding
averaged_trial_decoding.summary: Decoding movement information by averaging neural activity across multiple trials.

neural_decoding_algorithms.label: Neural Decoding Algorithms
neural_decoding_algorithms.summary: Computational methods used to extract movement information from neural activity.

calibration_phase.label: Calibration Phase
calibration_phase.summary: Establishing the relationship between neural activity and movement using statistical models.

ongoing_use_phase.label: Ongoing Use Phase
ongoing_use_phase.summary: Using the calibrated statistical model to decode movement from new neural activity.

discrete_decoders.label: Discrete Decoders
discrete_decoders.summary: Algorithms that estimate one of several possible movement goals (classification problem).

population_activity_space.label: Population Activity Space
population_activity_space.summary: A multi-dimensional space where each axis represents the firing rate of a neuron.

decision_boundaries.label: Decision Boundaries
decision_boundaries.summary: Boundaries in the population activity space that separate different movement goals.

continuous_decoders.label: Continuous Decoders
continuous_decoders.summary: Algorithms that estimate the moment-by-moment details of a movement trajectory (regression problem).

decoding_methods.label: Decoding Methods
decoding_methods.summary: Techniques used to translate neural signals into control signals for external devices.

discrete_decoding.label: Discrete Decoding
discrete_decoding.summary: A decoding method that estimates a subject's intended movement goal based on neural activity during a defined period. It relies on pre-defined decision boundaries.

calibration_phase_discrete.label: Discrete Decoding - Calibration Phase
calibration_phase_discrete.summary: The phase where the system learns to associate neural activity patterns with specific movement goals. Decision boundaries are optimized during this phase.

ongoing_use_phase_discrete.label: Discrete Decoding - Ongoing Use Phase
ongoing_use_phase_discrete.summary: The phase where the system uses the learned decision boundaries to predict the movement goal based on new neural activity.

continuous_decoding.label: Continuous Decoding
continuous_decoding.summary: A decoding method that estimates moment-by-moment details of movements, such as position, velocity, and acceleration.

calibration_phase_continuous.label: Continuous Decoding - Calibration Phase
calibration_phase_continuous.summary: The phase where 'pushing vectors' are determined for each neuron, indicating how its activity influences movement velocity.

ongoing_use_phase_continuous.label: Continuous Decoding - Ongoing Use Phase
ongoing_use_phase_continuous.summary: The phase where pushing vectors are scaled by the number of spikes emitted by each neuron to decode movement velocity.

pushing_vectors.label: Pushing Vectors
pushing_vectors.summary: Vectors representing the influence of a neuron's activity on movement velocity. Magnitude and direction indicate the strength and direction of influence.

pva.label: Population Vector Algorithm (PVA)
pva.summary: An early continuous decoding algorithm that assigns pushing vectors along a neuron's preferred direction. Does not account for spiking noise.

ole.label: Optimal Linear Estimator (OLE)
ole.summary: A more accurate continuous decoding algorithm that incorporates the properties of spiking noise to determine pushing vectors.

temporal_smoothing.label: Temporal Smoothing
temporal_smoothing.summary: A technique to improve decoding accuracy by considering neural activity in the recent past, as movement velocity changes gradually over time.

kalman_filter.label: Kalman Filter
kalman_filter.summary: A statistical model used to estimate movement velocity by combining current neural activity with the estimated velocity from the previous time step. Widely used in BMIs.

neural_activity.label: Neural Activity
neural_activity.summary: The electrical signals generated by neurons, which are decoded to control BMIs.

velocity_decoding.label: Velocity Decoding
velocity_decoding.summary: Decoding of movement speed and direction from neural signals. Often used as a starting point for BMI design.

clinical_applications.label: Clinical Applications
clinical_applications.summary: The use of BMIs to restore function in patients with paralysis.

communication_bmi.label: Communication BMI
communication_bmi.summary: BMIs designed to allow patients to communicate by decoding their intended messages from neural activity.

information_transfer_rate.label: Information Transfer Rate (ITR)
information_transfer_rate.summary: A metric measuring how much information can be conveyed per unit time, typically in bits per second (bps).

activity_space.label: Activity Space
activity_space.summary: A multi-dimensional space where each axis represents the firing rate of a neuron. Neural activity defines a point in this space.

movement_goals.label: Movement Goals
movement_goals.summary: The intended targets or directions of movement that the decoder attempts to predict.

fixed_boundaries.label: Fixed Boundaries
fixed_boundaries.summary: The decision boundaries established during the calibration phase that remain constant during the ongoing use phase.

movement_prediction.label: Movement Prediction
movement_prediction.summary: The process of determining the intended movement goal based on the location of new neural activity within the decision boundaries.

pushing_vector_determination.label: Pushing Vector Determination
pushing_vector_determination.summary: The process of identifying how each neuron's activity influences movement velocity during the calibration phase.

vector_summation.label: Vector Summation
vector_summation.summary: The process of adding the scaled pushing vectors to determine the decoded movement velocity.

cursor_update.label: Cursor Update
cursor_update.summary: The process of updating the position of the BMI cursor (or limb) based on the decoded movement velocity.

preferred_direction.label: Preferred Direction
preferred_direction.summary: The direction of movement for which a neuron shows the highest level of activity.

spiking_noise_consideration.label: Spiking Noise Consideration
spiking_noise_consideration.summary: The incorporation of the variance and covariance of spiking noise into the decoding process to improve accuracy.

preparation_epoch.label: Preparation Epoch
preparation_epoch.summary: The period of neural activity occurring *before* the execution of a movement, used for decoding in discrete BMIs.

velocity_estimation.label: Velocity Estimation
velocity_estimation.summary: Using neural signals to estimate the velocity of a movement.

execution_epoch.label: Execution Epoch
execution_epoch.summary: The period of neural activity occurring *during* the execution of a movement, used for decoding in continuous BMIs.

v_kf.label: V-KF (Velocity Kalman Filter)
v_kf.summary: A Kalman filter calibrated using neural activity recorded during actual arm movements (open-loop control).

refit_kf.label: ReFIT-KF (Recalibrated Feedback Intention-Trained Kalman Filter)

itr.label: Information Transfer Rate (ITR)
itr.summary: A measure of the amount of information conveyed by the BMI per unit of time (bits/second). Increases with the number of targets, despite decreasing accuracy. (Fig 39-7B)
